title: Katz: Efficient Workflow Serving for Diffusion Models with Many Adapters
problem: Production T2I services struggle to efficiently serve diffusion models augmented with many ControlNet and LoRA adapters, where ControlNets introduce significant compute overhead while LoRAs are bottlenecked by loading latency.
motivation: Efficient multi-adapter diffusion model serving is critical for scalable production cloud services that need to support diverse image generation controls.
method: KATZ decouples ControlNets from the base model and deploys them as an independent, independently-scalable service on dedicated GPUs for caching and sharing. It employs bounded asynchronous loading to overlap LoRA loading with base model execution by a maximum of K steps while maintaining image quality. The system further accelerates base model execution across multiple GPUs using latent parallelism.
key_novelty: Removing ControlNets from the critical path by deploying them as an independently scalable microservice on dedicated GPUs.
contributions: ControlNet-as-a-Service architecture enabling decoupled, independently scalable ControlNet deployment
Bounded asynchronous LoRA loading that overlaps loading with base model execution while preserving image quality
Latent parallelism for efficient multi-GPU base model execution
7.8x latency reduction and 1.7x throughput improvement over state-of-the-art T2I serving systems
primary_theme: Efficient multi-adapter T2I serving through ControlNet decoupling
